question.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)$ given that its derivative ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the corresponding unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$ are as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\sqrt{3}\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,k,\,{T}^{′}(t)=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{2}\,i-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{2}\,k\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the derivative of the curve ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we find the magnitudes of ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${T}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{2})}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{(\frac{-\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{4}({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\frac{1}{2} \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(\sqrt{3})^{2}+(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)+3} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the curvature is 

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{(\frac{1}{2})}{2}=\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
